assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened a new observational window: the IceCube detector, a cubic-kilometre instrument in Antarctic ice, found a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, then pointed to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. This is exactly the kind of detector-driven discovery that matters most to me, with careful calibration and background rejection against atmospheric muons and neutrinos.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the cubic-kilometre ice concept and the collaboration; Karle is credited for leadership in construction and analysis. The two-name list is workable, but I recall that others (for example early AMANDA leaders and key analysts) have also been mentioned in the literature, and a hardware-versus-analysis split could be contested. I cannot verify this here.
assessment.maturity: Strong: the diffuse flux has been seen in several independent channels and in the same detector with different techniques; the source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) came later and are less independently confirmed by other experiments such as KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Source identification is still evolving and relies mostly on one experiment
Whether two names fairly capture the decisive contributions
Cosmic origin of the bulk of the flux remains open

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with a magic wavelength is a clear instrument invention. It gave fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and relativistic geodesy, and it points to a redefinition of the second. Great clarity and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2001-03 and realised it; Ye's group pushed the accuracy and stability to the frontier. This is a clean two-person attribution, though Ye also appears in other candidate groupings and Hall already received the 2005 prize for the frequency comb.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent labs worldwide have built lattice clocks that agree at the 1e-18 level, and clock comparisons are routine. Redefinition of the second is still pending, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap in the community with earlier clock and comb prizes (2005, 2012)
Whether Ye or other trapped-ion clock pioneers should be weighed alongside
Outside my own field, so I rely on AMO colleagues for credit details

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are a remarkable technical achievement: global VLBI at 1.3 mm, with calibration and imaging algorithms robust against systematics. They give direct strong-field tests of general relativity. Impact is both scientific and public.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over a very large collaboration. Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea, Doeleman led the EHT effort and the technical VLBI development, and Moran contributed decades of VLBI foundation and the SMA. The three-name limit is a real difficulty and any selection is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets (M87* in 2019, Sgr A* in 2022) and multi-epoch M87* data support the interpretation. Yet polarisation and jet-launching results are still developing, and the black-hole prize of 2020 reduces novelty slightly.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit cannot be cleanly cut to three
Image reconstruction is partly model-dependent
Possible perception of overlap with the 2020 black-hole prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays give a window on nanohertz gravitational waves from supermassive black-hole binaries or early-universe sources. Reaching the precision needed demanded decades of timing, instrument improvement and noise modelling. It would be an important new band after LIGO.
assessment.attribution: The result is collective (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA), and the proposed names represent leaders of different arrays; I am unsure these three capture the decisive contributions, and the idea originates with Hellings-Downs and Detweiler earlier.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view: the 2023 evidence for Hellings-Downs correlation is around 2-4 sigma and the astrophysical origin (binaries versus new physics) is unsettled. Combined datasets are expected to improve this within a few years.
uncertainties: Significance of the angular correlation is not yet a clear detection
Origin of the signal is unresolved
Credit is spread across several consortia and several decades

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced a precision map of CMB anisotropies and pinned down the age, composition and flatness of the Universe, establishing the standard LambdaCDM parameters at percent level. An outstanding instrument and data-analysis achievement, although much was refined later by Planck.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was the PI and led the mission, Page was a key instrument builder and designer of the radiometers, and Spergel led cosmological interpretation. This is a reasonable trio, although the COBE and cosmology prizes (2006, 2019) have already recognised the field.
assessment.maturity: Completely mature and confirmed independently by Planck, ACT and SPT. The risk is that recognition is late and the field has already been rewarded twice.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2006 and 2019 cosmology prizes
Planck largely superseded WMAP, which may weaken the case

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal and the subsequent ion-trap experiments by Blatt and others established controlled gates and entanglement with trapped ions, now a leading platform for quantum computation. Haroche and Wineland have already received the 2012 prize for single-system quantum control, but this adds the computing architecture.
assessment.attribution: The scheme was proposed by Cirac and Zoller in 1995, the leading experimental implementation in Innsbruck by Blatt; Wineland and Monroe also contributed experimentally and Wineland has the 2012 prize. The trio is natural but the experimental credit among Blatt, Monroe and Wineland's group is arguable.
assessment.maturity: High: multiple groups and companies demonstrate high-fidelity gates and small processors. However, scalable utility is not yet demonstrated and the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits just recognised quantum hardware, so timing is debatable.
uncertainties: Candidate B035 appears to be essentially the same credited trio, so this overlaps with it
Experimental credit versus Monroe and Wineland
Outside my own expertise, so I rely on colleagues

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform of flat bands with correlated insulators and superconductivity, and launched twistronics. Very high impact in the last decade, with a clean theory prediction followed by experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulating and superconducting states in 2018 (Cao et al.). Others, such as Dean and Young on moire platforms and Cao as first author, may deserve consideration. The three names are a plausible prediction-plus-experiment pairing.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, although the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated. It may be a few years early for a prize but is well on the path.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity is unresolved
Sample-to-sample variation is large
I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on weighting

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation peak is a standard ruler detected in galaxy clustering, and is now a pillar of precision cosmology and dark-energy constraints. It combines survey instrumentation (SDSS, 2dFGRS) with a clean physical prediction.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein and collaborators detected the peak in SDSS luminous red galaxies, while Cole, Peacock and the 2dFGRS team measured it at the same time. Theoretical foundations by Peebles, Yu and Sunyaev, Zeldovich precede this and the Nobel-eligible credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed in many surveys (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI) and in the CMB. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy keep it topical, but they are not yet established.
uncertainties: Theoretical antecedents complicate attribution
Cosmology has been recognised several times already
Observational credit is shared across two large surveys
